content.value_statement: Material 3 specifications can contain inconsistent values and unsupported platform assumptions. This skill supplies component references, exact tokens, and visual guidance for source-backed design decisions.
actual_capabilities: Guide component selection, anatomy, variants, placement, interaction states, and accessibility requirements.
Reference published typography, corner-radius, elevation, contrast, and motion token values.
Specify spatial and effects springs for expressive interactions.
Plan adaptive navigation and pane layouts across breakpoints.
Locate component diagrams and interface examples through the bundled visual caption index.
Distinguish Material guidance, Compose token provenance, and custom design decisions.
limitations: Platform references describe a captured release state and require verification against installed library versions.
Some token tables and measurements are absent from converted guideline text; Compose-derived values need explicit provenance.
Google reference images retain separate licenses and are not reusable product source assets.
Refresh scripts require Node.js and network access; image refresh needs path and destination hardening before use.

faq.question: Is M3 Expressive a replacement for Material 3?
faq.answer: No. It extends Material 3 with updated components, motion, typography, shape options, and expressive design tactics.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Does the skill provide implementation guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes component rules, token values, motion guidance, and platform references. Generated implementations still require testing.

faq.question: Are expressive features identical across platforms?
faq.answer: No. Compose, Android Views, Flutter, and web support differ. Check the platform reference and your installed library version.

faq.question: Does ordinary design work require network access?
faq.answer: Bundled references support local design work. Refresh scripts access Material Design and GitHub sources when explicitly run.

faq.question: Can the bundled images be reused in a product?
faq.answer: They are reference renders, not editable product assets. Google content retains separate licenses that must be checked before reuse.
